title: Public Financial Management (PFM) Consultant - Australia Fiji Health Program
description: Fiji Program Support Platform (FPSP) Short Term Role – commencing September 2026 to February 2027 Based in Suva, Fiji Its a locally engaged role - open to Fiji Nationals only. FPSP Overview: The Fiji Program Support Platform (FPSP, or the ‘Platform’) is a Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) investment that contributes to the delivery of Fiji’s national development priorities, in line with the Australia’s International Development Policy, the Fiji-Australia Vuvale Partnership and the Development Partnership Plan. The Platform delivers key bilateral programs, such as health, education, scholarships, social infrastructure, governance, climate and emergency preparedness and response. Platform activities identify and address climate risks, promote climate action, and gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) across and beyond the sector programs. The Platform has three functional Outcomes: The Platform has delivered its sector program outcomes, including through supporting strategic coherence, planning, partnerships management, data and learning across the portfolio of investments. The Platform has prioritised gender equality, disability-inclusive development, and climate and disaster resilience, in its systems and practices. This includes in how it undertakes sector programming and its engagement with selected Government of Fiji (GoF) agencies. The Platform administers timely and efficient programming that is: value for money; maximises use of local supply chains; and supports good governance, and public diplomacy, effective decision making and risk management. AFHP Overview: The Fiji Program Support Platform (the Platform) implements over fifty percent of Australia’s bilateral development support to Fiji across a range of sector programs in education, health, Australia Awards, disaster response, cyclone recovery, social infrastructure and technical assistance to improve public sector governance in Fiji. The Platform integrates cross-cutting themes, including gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI), climate and disaster resilience, across sectoral programs. In particular, the Platform seeks to strengthen program outcomes by better addressing the needs of targeted beneficiaries including those who are often marginalised. The Australian Government is supporting Fiji’s health sector through the Australia Fiji Health Program (AFHP, the Program) working with the Ministry of Health and Medical Services (MHMS). The program’s high-level End of Program Outcomes (EOPOs) are: Improved systems are used by MHMS and health workers for evidence-based planning and resource allocation (workforce and budget), clinical care, digital health and medical supply chains; and Targeted healthcare facilities equitably deliver improved primary health services, with a focus on sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) and non-communicable disease (NCD) services. The funding for the program is approximately AUD 45million over 9 years (5 years, with an option to extend a further 4 years) and delivered through a range of activities (interventions) to achieve the program’s objectives where implementation modalities include technical advice, procurement of technical services and goods, minor works and infrastructure upgrades, capacity building and training support, support to Ministry led initiatives and innovations, and grants to civil society organisations (CSOs). AFHP is designed to support the MHMS achieve the goals and objectives in its Strategic Plan and Annual Operational Plans, and AFHP’s workplans are targeted to support specific components of the Ministry’s plans. Recent natural disasters such as cyclones, and public health emergencies in Fiji including COVID-19 have highlighted major challenges for pandemic preparedness and response during epidemics and other health emergencies. In this context, around 10% of program funding will be allocated for MHMS to assign to emerging needs and priorities as they arise. Funding may be allocated toward preparedness and responses to public health emergencies, or related opportunities for reform and innovation. Position Summary: The Consultant will work closely with the PFM Adviser, the Ministry of Health and Medical Services (MHMS), and the Ministry of Finance (MoF) to strengthen public financial management systems within the health sector. The assignment will focus on the development of a sector-wide PFM framework, assessment of current systems, identification of reform priorities, and support for implementation planning and institutional capacity transfer. Key Deliverables: 1. PFM Diagnostic and Gap Analysis Report Conduct a targeted assessment of MHMS public financial management systems against relevant national and international standards, including PEFA benchmarks, the Fiji Financial Management Act and Regulations, Fiji Procurement Regulations, Public Sector Infrastructure Programme Guidelines, and recommendations from the World Bank Health Sector Review. The report will identify key strengths, critical bottlenecks, priority reform areas, risks, and recommended actions. Established baselines for all PFM related indicators in MHMS Strategic Plan and AFHP MERL Framework Timeline : Months 1-2 2. MHMS Public Financial Management Framework Develop a comprehensive MHMS PFM Framework that consolidates existing policies, procedures, governance arrangements, accountability mechanisms, and good practice requirements into a single reference document for the health sector. The framework will include: Governance and accountability arrangements Planning, budgeting and procurement alignment model Budget execution and commitment control framework Financial reporting and performance monitoring framework Internal controls and risk management framework Roles and responsibilities matrix Present the framework to the Permanent Secretary for Health and Senior Leadership Team for review and endorsement. Timeline : Months 3-5 3. PFM Reform Implementation Roadmap Develop a phased implementation roadmap to operationalise the MHMS PFM Framework. The roadmap will include: Short-term actions (0–12 months) Medium-term actions (1–3 years) Long-term reforms (3–5 years) Responsible units and accountabilities Performance indicators and milestones Sequencing and prioritisation of reforms Timeline : Month 6 4. Validation and Knowledge Transfer Facilitate stakeholder engagement, validation and institutionalisation of the framework and reform roadmap through workshops and knowledge transfer activities. Outputs will include: • Conduct a validation workshop • Stakeholder feedback and consultation report • Final package of approved frameworks, tools and implementation roadmap handed over to MHMS Timeline : Months 4–6 Key Working Relationships: Reporting to: PFM Adviser - AFHP Other: PS MHMS MHMS Finance and HR Division Ministry of Finance Senior Health Specialist - AFHP Selection Criteria: Qualifications Advanced degree in Public Financial Management, Economics, Accounting, Finance, Public Administration, or a related field. Professional certification such as CPA, CA, CFA, CIPFA, or equivalent is desirable. Experience Minimum of 10 years' progressively responsible experience in public financial management, including budgeting, expenditure management, public sector accounting, financial reporting, and fiscal oversight. Demonstrated experience working within Fiji's public financial management systems, regulatory environment, and institutional frameworks. Experience in donor-funded programs and familiarity with donor financing modalities, fiduciary risk management, and accountability requirements. Proven experience in organisational capacity strengthening, including training, coaching, and mentoring. Strong stakeholder engagement and facilitation experience, including working with senior government officials and development partners. Experience in the health sector is highly desirable. Desirable Experience working in Pacific Island Countries or similar small-island developing state contexts. Experience working on DFAT-funded programs or comparable international development initiatives Knowledge and Skills Strong knowledge of international good practice in public financial management, including planning, budgeting, procurement, financial reporting, internal controls, and performance monitoring. Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex financial information into practical policy and operational recommendations. Strong communication, facilitation, and report-writing skills, including the preparation of high-quality technical reports, policy briefs, and presentations. Ability to build effective relationships, influence decision-makers, and engage confidently with senior stakeholders. Understanding of health sector financing and public expenditure management is desirable. Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality outputs within agreed timeframes. How to Apply: Applications close on 10 September 2026. Please apply online by submitting a cover letter addressing how you meet the selection criteria of this role and an up-to-date comprehensive CV. #LI-AUSBRIT #LI-JR1

title: Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Specialist |WPP – APSP
description: Commencement: Late September/Early October 2026 Short-term role up to February 2027, with possibility of further work Hybrid: Port Moresby / Western Province, Papua New Guinea / Some remote work Open to all applicants About the Program A stable, prosperous, peaceful and resilient Papua New Guinea is critical to Australia’s interests. Australia is PNG’s largest development partner and a key partner on economic and security issues. The Australia–Papua New Guinea Subnational Program (APSP) includes an enabling Facility and four program activities: Western Province Partnership, Kokoda Initiative Partnership, Subnational Governance Implementation Plan, and Bougainville Partnership. Each activity has its own outcomes, theory of change, operating approach, and monitoring and evaluation system. The APSP Facility provides shared services to support delivery across all activities, including HR, finance and administration, safety and security, procurement and infrastructure, grants, fleet and transport, ICT, legal/contracts, GEDSI and safeguarding, communications, and MEL. Abt Associates manages APSP under a single contract through to 2030. The centralised model drives value for money through back-office efficiencies, keeps key policy priorities (gender, disability, subnational governance and climate change) consistent across activities, and supports learning and adaptation between programs About the Opportunity The Western Province Partnership (WPP) is a component of the APSP. WPP supports Australia and Western Province to foster stronger ties and better coordination to improve human and economic development, enabling infrastructure and regional security. The WPP is also nested under the Australia-PNG Western Province Strategy (2022-2030). The WPP works toward the realisation of the following end of program outcomes (EOPO) by 2030: Women and men participating in program activities have diversified livelihoods from agriculture and fisheries. Targeted communities collaborate to strengthen welfare, production, and resilience. Women contribute to decision-making and take on leadership roles in targeted provincial, district, and community structures. Policy and practice at provincial and district levels are directed towards delivery of minimum priority services. WPP is delivered through the following program components: Water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) Community grants Economic Initiatives Program Gender Empowerment and Advocacy Program Ranger program Provincial capacity development Disability support services Abt’s Papua New Guinea headquarters are in Port Moresby; however, WPP operates primarily from Daru, with a small satellite facility and office in Morehead. The program delivers across a broad geographic area, supporting activities in multiple remote locations across Western Province, mostly in South Fly District. Western Province is a challenging operating environment, with complex logistics driven by distance, limited transport infrastructure and weather-related access constraints Key responsibilities Reporting to the SGIP Team Leader, and working closely with the WPP Team Leader and Deputy Team Leader, the Specialist will: Review relevant WPP WASH documentation, including current activity plans, evaluation findings, management responses, workplans, monitoring data, implementation lessons, and any available government WASH plans or strategies. Prepare a concise consultation plan, including key questions, stakeholder groups, consultation methods, timeline and expected outputs. Facilitate consultations through workshops, interviews or other appropriate formats with DFAT/Australian High Commission sector teams, the managing contractor, implementing partners, and relevant Government of Papua New Guinea and Western Province counterparts. Capture stakeholder views on WASH priorities, delivery constraints, sustainability requirements, governance arrangements, climate resilience, GEDSI, safeguarding, logistics, procurement considerations and value for money. Analyse lessons from current and recent WASH implementation, including the suitability of objectives, outcome areas, statements of requirement, implementation arrangements, deliverables, governance arrangements, risk settings, grant management approaches and selection criteria. Identify the core service areas that should be covered under the 2027–2030 WASH grant opportunity, including water supply, sanitation and hygiene behaviour change, operations and maintenance, WASH governance, disaster preparedness, monitoring, learning and adaptive management. Advise on how the grant opportunity should address sustainability of water services, including community ownership, maintenance systems, spare parts, financing, government roles and subnational service delivery arrangements. Advise on how the grant opportunity should address climate and disaster resilience, including drought, flooding, water security, emergency response arrangements and protection of water sources. In consultation with the APSP GEDSI Lead, advise on how GEDSI, safeguarding and Do No Harm requirements should be integrated into the grant opportunity, including meaningful participation of women and people with disabilities in WASH planning and decision-making. Translate consultation findings into a clear scope of works and statement of requirements that can be tested through an open tender process. In consultation with the Abt Grants Team, define expected provider capabilities, including technical WASH expertise, remote delivery capacity, community engagement, government engagement, safeguards, GEDSI integration, monitoring and reporting, financial management and ability to work through subnational systems. Identify delivery assumptions, dependencies, constraints and risks that should be reflected in the grant opportunity guidelines and related procurement documents. Provide advice on appropriate grant deliverables, including inception requirements, workplans, budgets, risk management, safeguarding, environmental and social safeguards, MERL, reporting and participation in WPP review and reflection processes. Work with WPP, APSP procurement and contracts staff, grants staff and DFAT as required to refine the scope and ensure it is suitable for an open grant opportunity. Prepare concise written outputs, including consultation notes, a findings summary, an annotated outline of the grant opportunity guidelines, and draft technical content for inclusion in the grant opportunity. Consultation plan, including proposed stakeholders, consultation questions, method, schedule and outputs. Summary of key findings from stakeholder consultations, including priority issues, design implications and areas requiring decision by WPP, APSP or DFAT. Annotated outline for the WASH grant opportunity guidelines, showing the proposed structure and key content for each section. Draft technical content for the 2027–2030 WASH grant opportunity, including objectives, scope of works, statement of requirements, core service areas, implementation arrangements, deliverables, assumptions, risks, safeguards, GEDSI, MERL and expected provider capabilities. Conduct and oversee literature screening, data extraction, study quality assessment, risk-of-bias evaluations, and evidence integration activities. Apply epidemiologic principles and evidence evaluation frameworks to assess causality, strength of evidence, and potential public health impacts. Evaluate study design, exposure assessment methodologies, confounding factors, statistical approaches, and other elements influencing study validity. Collaborate with toxicologists, exposure scientists, pathologists, and statisticians to integrate human, animal, and mechanistic evidence into comprehensive health hazard assessments. Support scientific briefings, presentations, and interactions with the client federal partners, advisory committees, and external peer reviewers. Contribute to quality assurance activities to ensure scientific rigor, methodological consistency, and regulatory compliance across all project deliverables. Provide technical mentorship and guidance to junior epidemiologists, analysts, and research staff. Evaluate and utilize innovative approaches, including AI-enabled literature review tools, machine learning applications, natural language processing technologies, and data visualization methods to enhance evidence review and synthesis processes. Support project planning, technical risk management, and achievement of contract milestones and deliverables. Strong expertise in study design, causal inference, risk-of-bias assessment, and interpretation of epidemiologic evidence. Experience evaluating observational studies, cohort studies, case-control studies, cross-sectional analyses, and environmental health investigations. Knowledge of systematic review methodologies, evidence evaluation frameworks, and health hazard assessment approaches. Experience integrating epidemiologic findings with toxicological, exposure, and mechanistic evidence. Proven scientific writing experience, including peer-reviewed publications, technical reports, regulatory documents, or scientific assessments. Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills. Experience working as part of multidisciplinary scientific teams. Experience supporting NIEHS, NTP, EPA, CDC, NIH, FDA, or other federal health agencies. Experience conducting quantitative evidence synthesis, meta-analysis, or advanced epidemiologic modeling. Knowledge of statistical software and analytical tools such as R, SAS, Stata, or Python. title: Chief of Party - DRC Malaria Activity
description: The Opportunity Under the supervision of the U.S.-based Project Management Director, the Chief of Party (COP) manages, and supervises the successful implementation of the Abt Global Central Mechanism in the Democratic Republic of Congo and acts as the primary liaison between the project and the local U.S. Department of State, the National Malaria Program (NMP), Ministry of Health, other government agencies, and various other malaria stakeholders in-country. The COP provides overall strategic direction, operations management, technical leadership, and financial and administrative compliance for all project activities to assure milestones are completed on-time, and within budget. The Abt Global Central Mechanism supports malaria vector control and HIV/AIDS service delivery in 14 partner countries, with the goal of improving health outcomes for target populations while strengthening the planning, data management, and implementation capacity of host-country governments and local institutions. The project sustains uninterrupted malaria vector control interventions, including insecticide-treated net (ITN) distribution, indoor residual spraying (IRS), and spatial emanators, as well as HIV prevention, testing, and treatment services. Across partner countries, the project identifies opportunities to align and transition vector control data collection to national Health Management Information System (HMIS)/DHIS2 platforms. It also strengthens HIV laboratory referral and quality management systems and supports entomological and insecticide-resistance surveillance, including monitoring for Anopheles stephensi , in priority countries. In collaboration with government counterparts, the project identifies functions for transition and provides support to advance government memorandum of understanding (MOU) objectives. This activity runs for 9 months from January 1, 2027 through September 30, 2027. Core Responsibilities Represents Abt Global and the Project to the Ministry of Health (MOH), the NMP, the U.S. Embassy, and other key stakeholders. Carries full authority and accountability for activity decisions, as delegated by the U.S.-based Project Management Director. Sets and pursues a results-oriented program strategy in coordination with the project team and in consultation with the MOH, NMP, U.S. Embassy, other partners and stakeholders. Lead day-to-day execution of the firm fixed award, performance-based program, ensuring all activities, contractual milestones, acceptance criteria, and payment triggers are achieved on schedule. Manage competing priorities while maintaining full compliance with the negotiated statement of work and other contract requirements. Establish country team milestone-progress reviews to confirm that performance is on track to meet milestones. Escalate potential milestone failures, scope growth, funding pressures, and other contract-impacting issues promptly. Control scope through disciplined management and formal authorization of any changes affecting milestones, schedule, resources, or budget. Leads the development, achievement and production of all milestones, including but not limited to reports (e.g. country work plans, vector control summary reports, forecasting and procurement plans, etc) and project activities (e.g. start up activities, trainings, vector control tool deployment, etc). Develops and leads a country-specific transition discussion with NMP/government partners to determine priorities and identify gaps and develops a transition plan based on feedback and discussions. Ensures that safeguarding best practices are incorporated in all project activities from the design stage and that all staff are held accountable for enforcing safeguarding measures at every level. Supervises and mentors the project’s Senior Managers, such as the Integrated Vector Control Manager, Finance and Administration Manager, and others as applicable. Ensures that all country staff, , subcontractors and consultants understand their roles and responsibilities to ensure compliance with contract requirements, Department of State and Abt policies and procedures. Ensures that project budget projections, expenditure, tracking and reporting are in accordance with the project milestones and Abt Global requirements, procedures and practices. Ensures that lessons learned and best practices are documented and shared. Maintains regular communication with Abt Headquarters team, regarding project updates, issues and general project management aspects. Uphold the highest ethical standards and an ability to handle sensitive information with the utmost discretion. What We Value Bachelor’s Degree + 12 years, or master’s degree + 10 years , or PhD+ 8 years Master’s degree (minimum), or a Doctorate Degree (desirable), in Public Health/Health Administration (or other relevant health specialization) or Business Administration. 8 years of relevant international health experience. Significant experience in malaria prevention and control desired At least 3+ years of senior project management experience in large international health programs. Demonstrated experience delivering contractual milestones tied to client acceptance strongly preferred. Strong understanding of cost, schedule, scope, risk, and quality management. Experience managing fixed-award, firm fixed price or milestone-based engagements desired. Demonstrated leadership in management skills and ability to lead and motivate multidisciplinary, multicultural teams, ranging from 10 to 25 employees. Experience managing a fast paced, results-oriented, deadline-driven project. Significant ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with multiple stakeholders, including U.S. Department of State personnel, ministry officials, and other development partners. Experience developing and communicating a project vision, aligning key stakeholders around the vision, and assuring the vision is translated into efficiently implemented program activities. Strong ability to communicate and write reports and other professional documents in English. English professional fluency is required.
